chapter: The levee club and the St. Louis scene
title: One-night gig with Charlie Creath
summary: Invited to a jam session, Thomas got a call to play with Charlie Creath at an East St. Louis gig with his new initialed cornet. Creath told him he might be a trumpet player at 25.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Let me tell you about Charlie Creath. I'm going to get back to Shorty Baker, too. This is my boy, you know. So, we sat down one night -- about 5, 6 trumpet players, just a country boy, hmmm. Only tune I knew was a couple of tunes but I didn't do it on my own. I was invited. And it do make a an a difference. It's a difference between/amateur and/professional -- your thought. If I walked on Charlie Creath's bandstand or Dewey Jackson's bandstand, do you know what they do me -- throw me off bodily right in the middle of the street. Now, you dig this. (I think comes) from the whole teaching, too.
JT (2 of 1) 63

You know everything is musical if you think that way but the the approach, the person. So one night, I'm sitting there having drinks or two ... so a cat walks up to me and he says, "Hey, fellow." I said, "Who you talking to? Me." He say, "Yeah, you. You working tonight?" I said, "No, I'm not working tonight. I just closed on a Friday." I'm telling you.
Where had you closed?
At Green's place. on
Oh, at the levee?

JT: I think so. No, it couldn't have been Green's place, that's before Green's place. I folded at the roadhouse. Let me get these things together so we'll know. Green's another story. But, he said, "What are you doing tomorrow night?" Tomorrow night? "You working tomorrow night?" I said, NO, I'm not working tomorrow night. "Would you like to work with Charlie Creath?" "Charlie Creath?" Are you kidding. I just got my new horn, too, Stan, you know. I had a horn that said owner Joseph L. Thomas en-there-. Dig it.
Oh, you still got the old horn?
No, I got a new one.
Have you got a trumpet by now?
No, no, I got a cornet. I had a cornet but a beautiful one.
Good one.
JT (2 of 1) 64

Charlie Creath. He could have gotten me for free, really and truly, you know. So, my family just got this horn for me and I put a little money on it so I told Mr. Langford. (7...) wrapped in this tissue and all that kind of mess. And it was a corn horn, you know, CGM ... Joseph L. Thomas and, man I looked at that horn and all the things happening on the horn and beautiful. I told my me buddy I'm working with Charlie Creath, a new horn and working with Charlie Creath. You working with Charlie Creath. Now what do am I got to do? I got to go to East St. Louis. Now, East St. Louis, there were some fellows -- Connellsville, Collinsville Leon Collins and his brothers -- worked in Thomasville Illinois, Carbondale, around that territory there. Beautiful musicians, they were around my age, you know. And they'd meet me (wherever) meet me in East St. Louis. they had a gig ... rough town, rough town.
That's across the river.

Across the river. So I get this job to go over to Charlie Creath so we get over there and ... they're doing something something- and Charlie Creath walks in and he says to the cat, "You're the leader of the group. How does it go?" Say, "Everything is fine." In those days, you had to stand in line to get paid, at least I did.
Well, how big a band had he got then?
I guess around 10 pieces. That was not his regular band band. This is a gig man.
He'd have a whole lot of bands.
JT (2 of 1) 65

Oh, yeah, he had a whole lot of bands. So when he got to me I said -- now dig this I got this horn and I got my initials on it ... and I'm going along with the guys (?), you know -- so I said ... "Cresth" not the money now. Said, how did I do. He put the money where I could see it, said "in years," when I'm 25, you might be a trumpet player. "(?)" Tremendous guy. He had a chance to talk to me.
Did you work with him again? Oh, this was just a one short thing?
Yeah, ... one of those things.
